title: Lithos Property Bank
description: Defines the format of a Lithos property bank file. A property bank is a dictionary of reusable, named property definitions that individual note schemas can reference via '$ref: property_bank#/<name>'. The property bank itself is not a note schema — it has no 'name', 'extends', or 'excludes'.

properties.title: Property Definitions
properties.description: A map of named property definitions. Each key is the property name (lowercase, using only letters, digits, and underscores). Each value is a full property definition.

propertyNames.description: Property names must be lowercase and may only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

PropertyDefinition.title: Property Definition
PropertyDefinition.description: A full inline definition of a metadata property. The valid fields depend on the 'type' — see the type-specific variants below.

CommonFields.description: Fields present on every property definition regardless of type.

required.title: Required
required.description: Whether this property must be present in every note that uses a schema containing it. Defaults to false.

array.title: Array
array.description: Whether this property holds multiple values (a list) rather than a single value. Defaults to false.

StringProperty.title: String Property
StringProperty.description: A property that holds a text value. Optionally constrained to a fixed set of allowed values via 'enum', or validated against a regular expression via 'pattern'.

enum.title: Allowed Values
enum.description: Constrains the property to a fixed set of values. Supports three modes: (1) a plain array of strings when order is unimportant; (2) an ordered array of single-key objects mapping a positive integer to a value string, for explicit display order; (3) an ordered array of single-key objects mapping a stored value to a display label, for cases where the stored value and its human-readable label differ.

oneOf.title: Plain Value List
oneOf.description: An unordered set of allowed string values. Use when display order is unimportant or alphabetical order is acceptable. Example: ["education", "personal", "professional"]

oneOf.title: Ordered Numeric Map
oneOf.description: An ordered list of single-key objects where each key is a positive integer string encoding display position and the value is the stored string. Use when order has semantic meaning and the value is self-describing. Example: [{"1": "to_do"}, {"2": "in_progress"}, {"3": "done"}]

oneOf.title: Value-to-Label Map
oneOf.description: An ordered list of single-key objects where each key is the stored value and the value is the human-readable display label. Use when the stored value (snake_case) differs from what should be shown to the user. Example: [{"january": "January"}, {"february": "February"}]

pattern.title: Validation Pattern
pattern.description: A regular expression the property value must match. Use this for structured string formats like email addresses or identifiers.

NumberProperty.title: Number Property
NumberProperty.description: A property that holds a numeric value (integer or float). Optionally constrained by minimum, maximum, and step values.

step.title: Step
step.description: The increment/decrement step for UI controls. For example, 1.0 means whole numbers only.

BooleanProperty.title: Boolean Property
BooleanProperty.description: A property that holds a true/false value.

DateProperty.title: Date Property
DateProperty.description: A property that holds a date, time, or datetime value. The format string uses Go reference time notation: '2006-01-02' for dates, '15:04' for times, '2006-01-02T15:04' for datetimes.

format.title: Date Format
format.description: The display and parsing format for this date field, using Go reference time notation. Common formats: '2006-01-02' (ISO date), '2006-01-02T15:04' (local datetime), '2006' (year only), '15:04' (time only).

FileProperty.title: File Reference Property
FileProperty.description: A property that links to one or more other notes in the vault, identified by file path. Use 'directory' to restrict which vault folder(s) are valid targets. Use 'file_class' to require the linked note to have a specific schema.

directory.title: Target Directory
directory.description: A vault-relative path (or regex-style alternation of paths) specifying where valid link targets must reside. Use parentheses and pipe for alternatives, e.g. '(41_personal|42_education)/'. A trailing slash is required.

file_class.title: Required Schema
file_class.description: The name of the schema that the linked note must use. This constrains link targets to notes of a specific type.
